title: Judy Faulkner, Epic, and electronic health records
text:
This episode of Freakonomics Radio featured Judy Faulkner, the CEO of Epic, the Madison WI based electronic health records giant. Her rise and dominance of this critical market since 1978 is astounding, with historic competition and regulatory hurdles. Also, her business model is unique, with annual revenues of only about $5B, yet they control close to 80% of the EHR market in an industry that is 18% of the GDP. Importantly, this is not a publicly traded company, with 15,000 employee shareholders.

I found Faulkner's demeanor as a techie to be fascinating and down to earth. It is remarkable how they adapted the EHR over decades of profound change in the industry, having both a public-facing MyChart portal and an integrated EHR for both inpatient and outpatient care across the US (both the largest systems as well as smaller hospital practices). The strongest attribute is point-of-service accessibility and compatibility across institutions, more recently being web-enabled and voice friendly (i.e. "ambient AI"). Epic has historically lagged as a resource for clinical trials and research, though that is changing. How they will fare in the AI paradigm shift as a proprietary private shop remains to be seen. Also, there are several lawsuits alleging monopolistic actions.

Having grown up with Epic, including many frustrations with the many iterations of the system, I am stunned at its continued dominance and the independent private model, having resisted private equity!
